notes:
## 0.5.7

- If a file error prevents private audio from being erased, the meeting says so while playback and speaker separation keep it masked.

- Meeting mute and dictation privacy follow capture time, including delayed packets and key reports received within five seconds. Missing capture times use a 5.25-second arrival window; real device timing remains unproved.

- After separating a call, use minus or plus to rerun with a hint of 1 to 8 people besides you, while call audio is kept. If fewer speakers are found, the result says so; plus stays disabled after that shortfall or while manual merges apply, and Auto returns to the automatic count.
- Removing a near-miss question keeps that wrong spelling from being asked about after later dictations or a restart. Removing a plain word still allows later spelling questions; Reset all personalization clears removal memory.

- Calls made with an older speaker separator offer Separate again while their call audio is kept. Matching names and merges stay; uncertain matches stay unnamed, with any names not kept shown on your next visit if you left during the run and kept Dicta open.
- Fixed the Separate again offer after stopping or failing a rerun, and kept the names not kept notice visible during later progress updates.
- When re-separation changes speaker lines, old tasks mapped from Speaker N keep their owner unconfirmed mark on the page, in Copy and in export until confirmed or refreshed. Confirmations stay for unchanged lines or directly named owners, and renaming within the same separation still removes the normal mark.
- A failed or interrupted speaker save keeps labels, names and merges together.
- With Meetings on, you can enable call-note offers in Settings. Notes started from an offer can ask whether to stop after the app releases the microphone; only a click starts or stops notes.

- Learning shows one privacy line, aligned with its controls, and the spelling boxes, Add and Refresh line up in every theme. Privacy text explains that cloud cleanup and meeting summaries can send text and Dictionary words to Groq.
- Action items mark owners from automatic labels or the conversation as "owner unconfirmed", including in old summaries, Copy and export. Confirm the owner or name the speaker within the same separation to remove the mark; Ask marks exact mentions of these unconfirmed owners, while summary prose can still name people without a mark.
- Unnamed separated speakers offer name choices from spoken cues and renames in meetings you still keep, with a dismiss action for wrong names. Names stay on this PC as meeting text, with no voice matching; deleting the source meeting removes its names, while Learning reset keeps meeting data.
- Correcting or clearing a speaker name makes earlier named action owners unconfirmed again. Confirming an owner asks first, and saved Ask marks follow current names and confirmations.

- Learning asks before saving a word or changing a spelling. Spelling changes need three dictations containing the spelling across two days, then ask "Change Peterson to Petersen in every app?" with equal-weight Change and Keep buttons. A corrected repeat does not count toward the minimum. A misheard name said only twice, or only on one day, is never asked about and stays wrong.
- Learning and its list wait before accepting another click. List corrections name both spellings and their effect in every app. Removing a saved Learning correction from Learning or Dictionary removes it even if removal memory cannot be saved, with a warning that the suggestion may return. Dictionary Save refreshes Learning. Reset all personalization clears collected suggestions, remembered dictation and learning settings; Dictionary, saved corrections and History stay. The stored recent-window field stays for one release so older builds can still open Learning.
- Meeting transcripts check microphone echo per timed sentence using main's 0.6 correlation threshold and matching call words. Local, uncertain and untimed speech stays visible. A local sentence repeating five or more call words, at about the bleed level while the call is talking, can be hidden. Short replies need five distinct words for the 80% containment rule. Misheard call speech the mic picks up still appears under Me and reaches summaries and Ask, as on main. Call mute returns to main's whole-chunk omission rule; late answers remain, but mixed chunks can be omitted and long reference outages can still leak. Noise can still become invented words; the unproved speech gate remains removed.
- Meetings use your Dictionary in transcripts, notes, chapters, saved summaries, export and Ask, including old meetings. Summary and chapter reads preserve existing replacement outputs so names do not grow or cascade through rules. Reading never rewrites the saved text.
- Meeting summaries ask for specific decisions, tasks and unanswered questions. Links use a displayed transcript line inside the cited run, or a supporting neighbour within 30 seconds, that shares a content word with the item. This checks the location, not whether the item is true.
- Action items for known speakers name their owner once, and you show as "You" until renamed. Saved summaries, completed parts, Copy, export and Ask follow later names for Me and Speaker N. Separated speakers can get a one-click name suggestion from an introduction or address; its tooltip shows the mention time. Address suggestions never cross a sentence boundary, and the unseparated Them track gets none.
- Unnamed external speakers, including automatic Speaker N labels, cannot own tasks, even after a first-person commitment. A model-supplied name spoken as whole words with the same capitals stays as owner even without a speaker mapping; each word must look like a person's name. An owner taken from the conversation can be wrong. Its task text stays unchanged and can repeat the name, and its owner does not follow a later speaker rename until Regenerate. Ordinary words such as "Room 204" and joint tasks keep their wording. To assign a saved unassigned task after naming its speaker, use Regenerate, which sends another request to Groq.
- An empty summary reply keeps the previous summary and its notices, including when the meeting has notes. With no saved summary, user notes are kept and the overview says no summary was returned. An empty combine keeps the finished parts. An empty part no longer fails the whole run: other parts are kept and the summary says which part is missing. Saved speaker names replace exact labels without changing lower-case prose. Dictionary edits no longer count as recovered speech or a changed speaker when checking whether Refresh is needed. Live summary quality and token budgets remain unmeasured.

- Meetings show when at least a second of your mic was not recorded.
- Temporary pastes and recovered dictation copies request exclusion from Windows clipboard history and cloud sync. Consecutive failed pastes can restore Dicta's previous copy; private copies from other apps stay private.
- Light and Full's local fallback keep repeated openings, including "What it is, what it is not." and "Oh my god, oh my god it broke." False starts also stay; corrections such as "no wait" still work.
- The microphone now starts as soon as you press the dictation key. Saving the recording and its History row no longer comes first, and a quick tap saves nothing.
- Light loses fewer of your words. "You know" at the very start or end of what you said now stays, and so does a repeated "like" at the start.
- Full cleanup no longer changes what you said. A rewrite that drops or swaps a number, changes a unit, day, month or a name to a look-alike, drops a whole sentence or keeps under half your words now falls back to your own text. Names in your Dictionary or on screen stay allowed, and so does the same name spelled another way.
- Words you said stay in your text. "capital", "market cap", "trial period" and "colon cancer" are no longer treated as commands, "Can you delete that?" and "I don't want to delete that." no longer erase your sentence, "I mean" only corrects when the new number, date or name comes right after it, and lone letters such as the y in "Press y to confirm" always stay. Saying "hello period how are you" or "scratch that" on its own still works. Spoken "comma" now works at the end of a dictation, before "new line", before a question such as "how are you" and after a greeting before "I", as in "hello comma I hope you are well"; elsewhere it stays a word.
- "scratch that" no longer wipes a whole dictation when you said "period" earlier and it stayed a word: only what came after it goes. "I think so I mean I don't know." now stays as you said it.
- Your words only land in the field you dictated into. If you click another field or switch tabs while Dicta is working, it keeps the words on a card instead of pasting them in the wrong place.
- A key you are still holding, such as Shift, no longer turns the paste into a different shortcut. Dicta waits a moment for it to come up.
- A slow app now gets your words instead of whatever you had copied before. Dicta holds the words on the clipboard for 2 seconds when it cannot tell the paste landed, without delaying your next dictation, and anything you copy in that time is kept.
- A small pill with no words now stays up from when you release the key until your text goes out, including during Full cleanup. When nothing gets typed, Dicta says why: no words caught, a rule or spoken command cleared the text, or only filler words. A very short press with speech suggests holding longer; a stray tap stays silent. A failure from an earlier dictation now waits until your current one ends and is labelled as earlier, instead of disappearing. If a paste never shows up in a text field that has shown your earlier pastes, the recovery card offers your words.
- Meeting speakers get mixed up less often. A stretch where several people talk over each other no longer shows up as an extra speaker, and a change of speaker now lands on the pause between people instead of a word early or late.
- Report a problem is turned off for now. It comes back once reports go through a Dicta server instead of an address built into the app.
- A meeting summary that fails is tried again a few times and at the next start, and the Meetings list and the meeting page say it failed with Retry, even after a restart. A request Groq rejects is not retried on its own.
- A meeting recovered after Dicta stopped unexpectedly gets its speakers, chapters and automatic summary once the rest is transcribed, and Dicta says once that it recovered it.
- A stretch that fails to transcribe no longer leaves a meeting stuck as Recording: it ends, can be summarised, shows what is missing and is filled in when a retry succeeds. Live transcription stays ahead of queued retries.
- A note that can't be saved is shown on the meeting page and retried when its audio and privacy are known. Notes whose privacy is uncertain after a crash are left out and shown as not saved.
- A note whose audio was lost when Dicta stopped (muted, or never written) is shown on the meeting page as not saved instead of disappearing, and a note saved just before Dicta stopped is not saved twice.
- A meeting summary made before Dicta recovered more of the meeting says so and offers Refresh summary.
- In a call, the indicator warns when call audio stays silent for three minutes while you keep talking. Listening quietly does not trigger a mic warning.
- Dictation spans stay private across retries. After a crash, microphone audio whose privacy cannot be verified is left out with a notice. Delete cannot bring a meeting's text back through a retry.
- A model outage no longer exhausts note retries. When recovery gives up, the page says so and the saved transcript still gets its remaining processing. Undo keeps the recovered-audio warning with the earlier summary.

- After a crash, Dicta recovers microphone audio and unfinished notes whose privacy the recording journal can verify. Dictations stay private while meetings start and stop too. A short unverified tail stays out. Silent audio adds no warning, and other left-out audio is shown once with its duration. Gaps and missed notes appear once on the Transcript tab, and summary buttons and cards have room above them.

- A blocked meeting journal waits a second before retrying. Starting a meeting just after a dictation ends no longer leaves an open mute span. Copy transcript shows omitted microphone audio once with its duration.
